title: Week in Orbit
summary: A mix of strategic moves and technical challenges define this week in the space and defense sectors. From new launch targets in Sweden to the ongoing struggle with hypersonic testing, the landscape remains as complex as ever.

themes.title: European Launch Ambitions
themes.body: SSC Space and Firefly are eyeing a 2028 launch from Sweden’s Esrange, marking a notable push for European orbital capabilities. This could shift some dynamics in the launch market, especially if they manage to avoid the usual delays.

themes.title: Orbital Data Centers on the Rise
themes.body: Orbital's ambitious plan for 100,000 data centers in space is a bold bet on the future of data processing. If realized, this could redefine how we think about infrastructure beyond Earth.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion addition to space resilience indicates a growing recognition of the need for robust capabilities in an increasingly contested domain. This funding could bolster various initiatives, but the effectiveness will depend on execution.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Woes
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests highlight the complexities of advancing this technology. As the third quarter passes without success, stakeholders may need to reassess their timelines and expectations.
